rationale: Explore the concrete two-write boundary without claiming a consensus violation or applicable crash guarantee. Bootstrap and actual processRPC handlers create all critical receiver state; messages are controlled inputs rather than real remote elections. Background workers are omitted via the existing skipStartup test option, so full concurrent protocol reachability remains open. The StableStore wrapper fails one candidate-byte Set before mutation and otherwise delegates; a no-fault control uses the same receiver sequence. This experiment tests local failure/retry semantics only, not an obligation or system safety.
question: Under a conditional receiver-side history, does a failed candidate-byte write after successful vote-term persistence change how a later stale-log request is treated as a duplicate?
